newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 higher Monday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen $0.50 higher Monday.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were expected to be $0.50 per cwt higher on Monday with the market seen continuing to claw back from recent losses, livestock dealers said.
"We'll be higher on Monday. The run was real light today (Friday) and our weights are light. We are current with our marketings," one Illinois dealer said.

USDA estimated Friday that the average hog weight for the week to August 2 was 254 lbs, down from 255 lbs a week earlier and 256 lbs in the preceding week. It remained, however, above the 251 lbs recorded in the same week a year earlier.
Pork prices have also been recovering recently with USDA pork cut-out values Friday up $0.61 to $0.62 per cwt.
Dealers noted there should be a light kill on Monday with several plants closed for a floating holiday.

Hormel Food Corp's pork processing plant in Austin, Minn., and hog slaughtering plant in Fremont, Neb, will be closed along with Quality Pork Processing Inc's hog slaughter plant in Austin, which provides pork for Hormel's Austin plant. ConAgra Inc unit Swift and Co's pork plant in Worthington, Minn., will also be closed, company officials said.
